territorial_scope.description: Scope turns on development, deployment or operation of frontier models in whole or in part in New York state; the text does not require the developer to be located there.

evidence.quote: This article shall only apply to frontier models that are developed, deployed, or operating in whole or in part in New York state.

summary.short: Replaces Article 44-B of the New York General Business Law (RAISE Act) on frontier AI models. Requires frontier developers to publish safety frameworks and transparency reports and report critical safety incidents to a new DFS office; large developers file disclosure statements. Effective January 1, 2027, with the 2025 chapter.
summary.long: Repeals and replaces Article 44-B of the New York General Business Law, added by a 2025 chapter on frontier AI models, with the Responsible AI Safety and Education (RAISE) Act (bill A.9449/S.8828, recorded as signed Chapter 96 of 2026). It covers frontier models trained with more than 10^26 operations that are developed, deployed or operating in whole or in part in New York, excluding certain academic research (§§ 1420, 1425–1426). Large frontier developers (affiliates' prior-year revenue above $500 million) must publish and annually review a frontier AI framework and publish transparency reports before or concurrently with deploying new models; developers must avoid materially false or misleading statements about catastrophic risk (§ 1421). Developers must report critical safety incidents to a new DFS office within 72 hours, and disclose imminent-risk incidents to an authority within 24 hours (§ 1422). Large developers must file a disclosure statement and pay pro rata assessments (§ 1428). The attorney general may seek civil penalties of up to $1 million for a first violation and $3 million for subsequent violations; no private right of action (§ 1427). Section 3 sets the 2025 chapter's effective date at January 1, 2027.

notes: The document is bill A.9449 as it stands after substitution by S.8828 (Actions list, 02/25/2026), with passage by both houses and a 'SIGNED CHAP.96' entry on 03/27/2026; the registry status is adopted, not yet in force. The 2025 chapter (S.6953-B / A.6453-B) is not reproduced: its Article 44-B text, which this bill repeals, is not in the document, and its chapter number is not stated. Section 5 makes §§ 1, 2 and 4 take effect with the 2025 chapter, and the rest immediately; § 3 sets January 1, 2027. Internal inconsistency: § 1428(5) refers to a 'large frontier model', a term the article does not define (it defines 'frontier model'). § 1428(3)(c) uses a 5% beneficial-ownership threshold for private companies and a 50% threshold for publicly traded ones. The companion bill is S.8828 ('SAME AS S08828'). Obligations, thresholds, events and enforcement details are not coded in this Tier A pass beyond the entities and relations above.
